result.reason: The claim that no dental compliance software exists is wrong. result.competitor: Partly contradicts the claim. INFOCERT runs an NF203 'Livre de Police' (NF203 LP) software certification, built with AFNOR, for traders in second-hand goods, precious metals and used vehicles, so certified livre de police software exists. I could not see the certified products: the certificates.infocert.org directory did not render them. Creerentreprise says 'différents logiciels existent' that combine an electronic livre de police with real-time stock management. Scrap yards use weighing-bridge software for traceability (WinTruck.Net, METTLER TOLEDO DataBridge), but I found no evidence that these produce the 1649 bis declaration. Dépôt-vente POS and consignment tools exist (Capterra list, WikiCréa Excel), but I did not confirm French livre de police compliance for them. I found no free state tool for the register. I did not identify a dedicated French brocante or ferrailleur livre de police SaaS by name. Six product-focused searches turned up mostly law texts, so 'nothing does it' is not confirmed either.
result.duty:
Confirmed from secondary sources. Not checked on Légifrance; the service-public F23207 fetch failed with 503.
(1) Registre des objets mobiliers (livre de police), Code pénal R.321-1 ff. It applies to brocanteurs, antiquaires, dépôt-vente shops and anyone buying second-hand goods to resell. Entries are made daily and continuously. An electronic register has been allowed since 2013 if it is unalterable (chronological, unfalsifiable, numbered and dated pages, no official approval). Penalty up to 6 months' prison and a 30,000 EUR fine (creerentreprise, Fiducial, INFOCERT).
(2) CGI art. 1649 bis plus décret 2012-1322 (art. 344 GE ann. III). Habitual retail buyers of ferrous and non-ferrous metals file an annual declaration before 31 Jan with the DDFiP, listing each seller's identity and address and the yearly total bought from each. It is filled in from the livre de police. Not checked: whether it can be filed online on impots.gouv.fr, and whether it is still in force in 2026. A thetradehub.eu page labels CGI art. 1649 bis 'in force'.
(3) Precious metals: declaration to the bureau de garantie (CGI 534) and a livre de police (CGI 537) checked by Customs. Card, cheque or transfer payment has been required for retail gold purchases since 2011.
A proposition de loi on buying back precious-metal jewellery was registered on 21 Dec 2023; whether it passed was not checked. No 2024-2026 enforcement drive found.
result.market: Not reached. I found no register count of brocanteurs, dépôt-vente shops, ferrailleurs or gold buyers. FEDEREC (recycling federation) guides on achats au détail exist (2016, 2023 version hosted by Hoche Avocats), but the 2023 PDF was too large to fetch, so I have no counts from them.
result.reason: The duty is real, but only secondary sources confirm it: the registre des objets mobiliers under the Code pénal, the CGI art. 1649 bis annual declaration of retail metal purchases due before 31 Jan, and the Customs livre de police for precious metals (CGI 537). Fines reach 30,000 EUR. The claim that no product does the job is weakened. Creerentreprise says several logiciels already exist, and INFOCERT/AFNOR run a dedicated NF203 'livre de police' software certification. That means certified tools exist, though I could not name them. Most of the buyer groups (scrap yards, dépôt-vente shops) already use weighing or POS software. The register is tied to their daily operations, which makes a standalone register add-on hard to sell. Low score.

result.competitor: Free state tools: BRGM DUPLOS (declaration under the mining code, auto-filled Cerfa 13837) and DiaLog, a web app that replaces the free GesFor and produces forecast and technical cross-sections and drilling reports for export to the BSS. Ministry and DREAL end-of-works report templates exist, including the Qualiforage/GMI model. Searches turned up only generic estimating and quoting tools (Harvest) and geology software (RockWorks). No commercial French software was found for drilling-firm certification files or audit readiness. Accredited certifiers could not be confirmed, because the Qualit'EnR page returned 403. Qualit'EnR (Qualiforage for GMI) is a likely certifier and could offer its own process and tools.
result.duty: Confirmed and in force. Environment code L.241-2 (from loi APER of 10 March 2023, art. 83); decree 2025-884 of 2 Sept 2025; arrêté 'certification' of 18 March 2026 (JO 27 March 2026). Non-domestic water drilling firms must be certified by 31 Dec 2027 at the latest, under three modules: all water boreholes, polluted sites and soils, piezometers. First certification lasts 2 years, then 4-year renewals with on-site and document audits by Cofrac-accredited bodies (ISO/IEC 17065). Administrative fine up to 15,000 EUR per borehole drilled without certification. The firm pays for certification. Firms certified for GMI 'nappe' are certified by default for the 'all water boreholes' module. Domestic-borehole certification will get separate texts and a later consultation (not yet published). Borehole declaration reform under the loi de simplification art. 44 (all boreholes declared under the mining code by summer or end of 2027) still has no implementing texts. The auditor guide was still a draft out for consultation.
result.market: Not found. No register or statistic counting French water drilling firms turned up. Assemblée nationale written questions confirm the profession had no mandatory qualification before this reform. The likely size is a few hundred small firms, but that is unverified. Next sources to check: INSEE/Sirene NAF 43.13Z (which also includes geotechnical drilling), Qualit'EnR's Qualiforage directory, and the drilling trade syndicate.
result.reason: The duty is real. Decree 2025-884 and the arrêté of 18 March 2026 make certification mandatory for non-domestic water drillers by 31 Dec 2027, with Cofrac-accredited audits, on-site and document checks, renewals and fines up to 15,000 EUR per borehole. No commercial software for the job was found, but free BRGM DUPLOS/DiaLog already handles cross-sections, end-of-works reports and declarations. The certifier's own process will probably cover readiness. GMI-certified drillers (Qualiforage) are already certified for the main module. The market is small and uncounted, probably a few hundred firms. Demand is a one-off spike before 2027, then audits every 4 years. Domestic-borehole certification texts are still to come. The niche is thin, so a consultancy or template pack fits better than SaaS.

result.duty: Loi n° 2024-1039 (19 Nov 2024) and Art. L324-1-1 Code du tourisme. From 20 May 2026, anyone offering a meublé de tourisme anywhere in France must file a declaration and get a registration number, which must be shown on every listing. Platforms must take down listings that have no number. Décrets 2026-196 and 2026-197 of 19 Mar 2026 are in force. Art. 6 of décret 2026-196 (R.324-2-1 to R.324-2-4) covers data sent by intermediaries and refers to the number's validity and to a declarant who may differ from the host. I did not find the renewal interval. Main-residence status must be proven. Fines: DGE cites up to 5,000 EUR for a missing number. Secondary sources cite up to 10,000 EUR for failing to declare and 20,000 EUR for a false or fraudulent number. I did not check the 10,000 and 20,000 EUR figures in the legal text. The DGE page fetched seems to describe the old commune-by-commune regime.

result.reason: The duty is real. Under loi 2024-1039 and Art. L324-1-1 Code du tourisme, every tourist rental in France needs a declaration with a registration number from 20 May 2026, and the number must appear on each listing. But the national teleservice is not open yet (DGE says Q4 2026), so its bulk filing, API and agent options cannot be checked. Décret 2026-196 separates the declarant from the host, so filing through an agent looks possible. I did not find the renewal period, so the duty may be close to one-off. Hostcare already files for a flat 39 EUR on behalf of its conciergerie network, and PMS tools like Smoobu store the number and sync it to listings. Fines differ by source (5,000, 10,000 or 20,000 EUR).

result.competitor: The core job is already sold cheaply to small agencies. Galian, the main financial guarantor for agencies, sells a 'Registre LCB/FT' tool at 25 EUR TTC a month per agency (product sheet dated June 2026; I saw it in search results but the PDF returned HTTP 503). Editions Modelo / Septeo also sell a Registre LCB/FT, price not found. AP Scan (AP Solutions IO) was chosen by BSK Immobilier for 4,500 mandataires, so networks are already supplying tools to their agents. Konforme (GetApp listing) offers LCB-FT risk assessment, client screening and KYC files for real-estate professionals. Training is widely sold: Lefebvre Dalloz e-learning at 145-168 EUR HT, CCI Pays de la Loire at 400 EUR a day, JurisCampus. The only remaining gap is a small add-on (a training-proof register), which guarantors, networks and trainers can easily bundle.
result.duty: Real and in force. Under art. L561-2 CMF, estate agents fall under the anti-money-laundering rules (LCB-FT). Décret n° 2026-310 of 24 April 2026 (JO 25 April 2026, applies immediately per MySweetImmo) requires training from hire and at regular intervals. Training must fit the person's role and risk level and include a module on sanctions. Proof (programme, dates, attendance, certificates) must be kept for the time in role plus 5 years. Per MySweetImmo it covers agents, mandataires, property managers and syndics. Access to the beneficial-owner register uses a 3-year certificate (Monimmeuble). The DGCCRF inspects and the Commission nationale des sanctions (CNS) sanctions; a CNS estate-agency decision of 11 March 2026 exists on economie.gouv.fr. Per CNS context, penalties go up to EUR 5m, a practice ban or card withdrawal, and publication. I did not check the decree text on Légifrance. Not verified: the CNS decision of 22 April 2026 and the 210,000 EUR fine of 27 May 2026.
result.market: No official count found. About 160,000 people work in the sector, salaried staff and mandataires combined (2026 market-study blog). Estimates of independent mandataires range from 38,000 to 45,000 (Observatoire de la franchise, undated; LinkedIn post for 2024). iad France alone has about 13,600-15,000 mandataires. Network mandataires are mostly covered by their network's tools. Card-holding agencies number in the tens of thousands; no exact figure was found (the CCI register was not queried).
result.reason: The duty is real, recurring and enforced: the April 2026 decree on proof of training, CNS sanctions, DGCCRF inspections. But the core job is already covered. Galian, the guarantor most agencies already pay, sells a LCB-FT register at 25 EUR a month per agency. Modelo/Septeo and Konforme also sell registers or KYC tools. Networks such as BSK give AP Scan to their 4,500 mandataires. Mandataires inside networks are reached through the network, not as individual buyers. Willingness to pay beyond 25 EUR a month is doubtful, and training providers can bundle attendance certificates. What is left is a thin niche, the training-proof register, which incumbents can easily add.

result.duty: Arrêté of 23 June 2026 (published JO 26 June 2026, JORFTEXT000054311368) changes the arrêté of 1 Dec 2015 on RGE criteria. From about 26 July 2026: random RGE audits, stronger sanctions and a simpler 4-yearly review. Per Selectra only, not checked on Légifrance: suspension up to 24 months, mandatory withdrawal after 2 controls with major non-conformities, a documentary audit plus site visit, and a 4-year claims analysis. From 1 March 2027: RGE VAE (3 compliant audited sites) and the attestation chantier. Existing Qualibat practice: an audit within 2 years of award, 2 chantier description sheets, proof of the earlier audit, an annual follow-up questionnaire, and a review every 4 years. RGE conditions customer access to MaPrimeRénov', CEE, éco-PTZ and the 5.5% VAT rate. The arrêté text itself was not opened.

result.reason: The reform is real. The arrêté of 23 June 2026 (JO 26 June 2026, JORFTEXT000054311368) changes the 2015 RGE arrêté. Random audits and graded sanctions apply from about 26 July 2026; VAE and the attestation chantier apply from 1 March 2027. RGE is not a licence to trade, but customers need it to get MaPrimeRénov', CEE and éco-PTZ, so in practice firms must hold it. I found no dedicated audit-readiness software. But Qualibat's online espace entreprise (about 50,000 accounts) and Qualit'EnR's compte pro already handle the filing, and CAPEB sells audit-prep training. Pain is episodic: an annual questionnaire, one audit per family of works every 4 years, and a 4-yearly review. Willingness to pay is likely low. Without a solid product, this is mostly photo and document storage.

result.competitor: No dental-specific compliance or registre SaaS was found in 6 French searches. Partial substitutes: (1) external radioprotection firms (OCRs), which act as the cabinet's adviser on contract; ASNR letters show them advising cabinets, and in one case the accredited external-QC body kept the only CQE schedule. They cover much of the core job as a done-for-you service. (2) PCR Assistant by LORYON SARL, a radioprotection digitisation tool with dashboards and email/SMS reminders, aimed at approved bodies and inspectors, price on request (hellopro listing). (3) ASCND, formerly ABGX/C2i Santé Xview, radioprotection management software for the medical sector; its current offer was not verified. Dental practice-management suites (Logosw, Julie and others) were not checked for compliance modules (not_reached). Trackdéchets is a free state tool for hazardous-waste and DASRI tracking forms.
result.duty: Confirmed and in force. The ANSM decision of 8 Dec 2008 (with art. R.5212-28 of the Code de la santé publique) requires dental X-ray QC: quarterly internal QC, an annual external audit of internal QC, and external QC every 5 years on the anniversary date (±3 months). Results go in a registre des opérations kept with an equipment inventory. ASNR letters from 2025-2026 (INSNP-LYO-2026-0514, INSNP-LYO-2025-0491, INSNP-BDX-2025-0098) cite non-conformities for missed quarterly CQI, which trigger a re-inspection within 12 months. They also cite a CBCT installed in 2017 whose initial CQE was only done in Dec 2025, and missing training certificates. The cabinet must designate a radiation-protection adviser (conseiller en radioprotection, still often called PCR) under Code du travail R.4451. The claim cites R.4451-103; the adviser articles are around R.4451-112 to 124, so that article number is unverified. Waste rules also apply. For DASRI, a contract is required, with a pickup voucher plus an annual summary under 5 kg/month or a CERFA bordereau above that; records are kept 3 years. DASRI traceability on Trackdéchets has been mandatory since 2023 per a DREAL fiche, but whether producers under 5 kg/month are covered was not verified. Amalgam waste falls under the arrêté of 30 March 1998. Sanctions are inspection follow-up letters, re-inspections, and for hygiene failures administrative closure (a 2025 prefecture act in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region).
result.market: DREES counted 48,700 active dental surgeons on 1 Jan 2026 (47,600 in 2025). About 74% work only in private practice; 56% are in group practices, 21.7% practise alone and 15.9% work in health centres (Xerfi). No public count of cabinets was found; an estimate of roughly 25,000 to 35,000 sites follows from the group-practice share but is unverified. Nearly all sites run intraoral X-ray equipment, and many also have a panoramic or CBCT unit.
result.reason: The duty is real and enforced. ASNR inspection letters from 2025-2026 cite the ANSM decision of 8 Dec 2008, which requires quarterly internal QC, an annual audit, external QC every 5 years (within ±3 months) and a registre des opérations. They flag late controls, untraced CQE and missing training certificates. No dental-specific compliance SaaS was found. However, external radioprotection firms (OCRs) already act as the cabinet's radiation-protection adviser and largely do the core job as a service. PCR tools exist for professionals: PCR Assistant (Loryon) and ASCND, formerly ABGX/C2i Xview. Each cabinet faces about 4 to 6 events a year and low money pain. The buyer is reachable through MACSF, the ADF and the Ordre. Could widen to sterilisation logs (ARS closures), but it is mostly a checklist.

Duty is real. Penal Code L.321-7 and R.321-1 ff. require second-hand dealers to keep a register (electronic allowed if unalterable, no approval scheme). Metals buyers must file the CGI 1649 bis annual declaration by 31 Jan, electronically (form 2093-T-SD, tiers-déclarant file spec). Fine up to 30,000 EUR is only from a secondary source. I found no dedicated brocanteur or metals product, though InfoCert sells an NF203 livre de police, so competition is not fully excluded. Market is small, about 14,500 firms (a market study, unsourced), and the base is shrinking. Pain is low and paper registers cost 25-50 EUR. Legal acceptance of software is uncertain. The metals filing is a niche but a real hook.

Duty is real. Reg. 2025/2650 sets application at 30 Dec 2026 (medium/large) and 30 Jun 2027 (micro/small and natural persons). The Commission's 4 May 2026 review did not reopen the text, per secondary sources, so the CMS "30 Dec 2027" date looks wrong. Only the first placer files a DDS, and downstream traders are exempt, so the buyer pool is small. The simplified declaration covers micro/small primary operators in low-risk countries, not importers. Freyr says the timber provisions are postponed to 2029, and the SGS guide says the EUTR still applies to timber, so timber is a weak segment. Competition is not clear: Coolset markets an SME guide, osapiens offers TRACES integration, and vendors are many. I did not count French direct importers, did not read the OJ text, and did not confirm penalties. Low score: a small niche, weak frequency, and crowded vendors.

Duty is real: the annual update is due within 2 months of the AGM that approves the accounts. Anah can impose an astreinte up to 20 EUR per lot per week after a one-month formal notice, and subsidies can be blocked (ANIL). A volunteer syndic is the one case where the astreinte can be passed on to co-owners. The portal is free and declarative, and has webservices for management software. I found no public tool that auto-files for volunteers, but I could not check Matera or similar tools, so competition is unverified. Market: about 760k copropriétés in the registry. About 31.9k volunteer syndics with 255k lots were registered at 1 Jan 2022, a thin and unpaying niche. The new fields start Jan 2028, not Feb 2027 as the claim says. Willingness to pay is weak, and the update takes one form a year.

result.duty: Monthly statistical declarations (états) of flows and stocks by collecteurs/producteurs grainiers to FranceAgriMer, plus comptabilité matières; electronic filing mandatory since 2017. Penalty not verified.
result.reason: The duty is real. Collectors must keep a comptabilité matières and send monthly "états" (entries, exits, stocks) to FranceAgriMer. The 2012 note extended the stock scope to include négoce stocks. But a free state tool already does the core job. Since 1 Sept 2017 declarations must be filed online in FranceAgriMer's VISIOGrains application, either by web entry or by an ebXML file upload. A small collector can file free of charge, so the only gap left is an ERP-to-ebXML export, which is a thin niche. Not verified: the penalty, the current legal text, the number of collectors, and any commercial vendor. Market size is small (a few hundred collectors, mostly co-operatives and large traders), and the buyers already run grain ERPs.

The duty is real: L'Officiel des Métiers cites art. 27 of law n° 2026-534 of 25 June 2026, which requires SEFi with certified geolocation by 1 Jan 2027. A Conseil d'État decree is still pending, and no sanctions are stated. The Assurance maladie TSP form already requires a software publisher's attestation of a SEFi-enabled, CNDA-certified geolocation setup. That makes this a certified-vendor market. A solo founder would face the same certification barrier as K08, and existing ambulance-software publishers are the likely incumbents. I did not identify vendor names; searches for them returned nothing useful. About 60% of firms already comply. Indy offers free invoicing only. No firm count was found. The pain is real and the duty is mandatory, but a new entrant cannot realistically win.

The duty is real. SADs are one ESSMS category, assessed every 5 years under the HAS framework (fiche of March 2026), by Cofrac-accredited bodies chosen by the service, at about 7,000 EUR per assessment. The authority sets the schedule and the assessment feeds authorisation renewal. The software job is limited to preparation, self-assessment and action plans. Existing quality software (Ageval, QHSE tools) already targets HAS preparation, though I found none specific to SAD. I did not find a national count of SADs, so market size is not established. Buyers are often federated, departmental or municipal bodies that buy through procurement, and the evaluation itself cannot be replaced by software. The task did not ask for penalty details and I did not verify them. The score stays low.

The duty is real. CGCT R.2333-51 requires a per-stay register. Declarations go to each commune or EPCI portal, often monthly before the 10th (Mulhouse, Rouen), and zero declarations are required. A 10% departmental surcharge applies from 1 Jan 2026. No tool found consolidates filings across communes. Weak points: platform collection (FARITAS, décret 2024-612, a 3-year experiment) shrinks the hosts' direct burden. Commune portals are free. Chekin and PMS tools calculate the tax and export reports. Trackeet serves collectivités, not hosts. The niche of multi-commune hosts is small, and filing on each portal likely can't be automated. I found no business-count statistic (not_reached). Competitor depth was limited to 2 searches.

result.duty: Hazardous waste traceability (BSD on Trackdéchets since 2022, with the used-oil exemption contested), chronological waste register, and the PIEC duty to offer reused parts (decree 2016-703, extended to two-wheelers on 1 Oct 2024)
result.market: ANFA, from INSEE data for 2023: about 145k firms in the automotive services branch, of which about 73% are trade and repair. Another site claims 104k for the sector. The 60k independent garages figure is not verified.
result.reason: The duties exist but are thin for a paid add-on. Garages hold hazardous waste (used oil) and must keep a register. Used-oil BSD handling is contested: a 2024 DREAL deck says used oils are no longer exempt from the BSD, while another extract says handing oil to an approved collector is excluded. Trackdéchets is free and the collector usually issues the BSD, so the garage's work is small. The PIEC duty (decree 2016-703, extended to two-wheelers from 1 Oct 2024) is only a duty to offer and inform, with no recurring filing. I found no DMS with native Trackdéchets integration, but I only searched, so this is unconfirmed. Waste-software vendors such as Kerlog are the closest alternative, priced at roughly 200 to 2,500 EUR a month per one site. Market size: ANFA gives about 145k firms in the whole automotive branch, and the 60k garages figure is unverified. A 3 reflects weak pain and low willingness to pay.
